content.text: Kleurenwiezen (Belgian Colour Whist) is the national card game of Belgium. It is a highly competitive trick-taking game where players bid to decide the contract (objective) for the round. Contracts range from winning most tricks with a partner to winning all tricks solo ('Abondance') or even winning zero tricks ('MisÃ¨re'). It is characterized by its complex bidding hierarchy and the social use of specific 'whist' signals.

Derived from 18th-century Whist and influenced by English Solo Whist. It became a distinct Belgian variant in the late 19th century, with the addition of more complex bidding labels like 'Troel' and 'Miserie'.
4 players playing individually until partnerships are formed during bidding.
Standard 52-card deck. Aces are high, 2s are low.
